Why, for a flat packing pad
Weather, ozone, UV, water and steam, and it stays flexible cold. Creeps more than natural rubber under sustained load, so allow for it in the deflection
Where the pad carries sustained load. Best fatigue resistance, highest resilience and least creep of the eight, so the gap stays held. Not for oil, and it perishes in prolonged sunlight
The compromise where the pad is both loaded and exposed — good fatigue life with reasonable weathering
Where the pad sits in oil. Poor ozone resistance, so not for an exposed position
Low-cost enclosed packing. Fatigue life below natural rubber and no oil resistance
High temperature. Low tear strength and poor fatigue resistance make it a weak choice under load
Expensive sealing compounds with no fatigue or creep advantage in a packing pad

The compound is not what makes one pad different from another — the shape is. Any pad in this range can be moulded in any of the eight compounds we mix, so tell us the duty and we will name the material.
Hardness will not tell you how it behaves

Rubber bulges rather than compresses, so a thin wide pad is far stiffer than a thick narrow one of the same compound. Send the load and the deflection you can allow, and we set the shape and the hardness together.
Weather or load — they pull apart

EPDM survives sunlight and ozone; natural rubber holds a gap without creeping. Where the pad is exposed and loaded we quote neoprene and explain the trade rather than defaulting to whichever we mixed last.
Holes moulded in, not punched after
Fixing holes formed in the tool are cleaner and stronger than holes cut afterwards, and the pad keeps its full section around them. Send the bolt pattern with the outline.

What is the minimum order quantity for this part?

We supply in bulk. The minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, or quoted against the part where geometry or tooling makes that unrealistic. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum.
Can you match a competitor specification or reverse-engineer an existing part?

Yes — but send the load as well as the pad. A pad taken out of service has crept and measures thinner than it was moulded, so copying its dimensions reproduces a part that is already part-worn. We work back from the gap it has to hold and what sits on it.
What file formats do you accept for drawings?

PDF, DWG and DXF. An outline with the bolt pattern marked is enough — add the load per pad and the deflection you can allow, and hardness becomes our output rather than your input. A 3D model is not required for a flat pad.
Do you provide material test reports with each shipment?

Yes. Material test reports, dimensional inspection sheets and a certificate of conformance ship with every consignment. Hardness, tensile to ASTM D412 and compression set to ASTM D395 Method B are tested in-house, and load-deflection is checked on batch samples against the approved drawing.
What are your payment and delivery terms for international orders?
TT and LC accepted, discussed per order. Ex-works Nashik or FOB Nhava Sheva. Commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin are issued with every consignment. Pads ship flat and unloaded.
